Tidewater Gazette

Notices to mariners and harbor users

What changes at the outer moorings

The port office sets its dues each autumn from the cost of dredging the channels and keeping the lights, divided among the vessels expected to call over the winter. This year the outer moorings, which lie beyond the breakwater and take the weather first, are priced apart from the inner basin for the first time.

When the new dues apply

Vessels under twenty metres pay as they did last winter. Larger vessels pay a little more per metre, because the outer chains are inspected twice as often. The new dues apply from the first of the month after the notice is posted at the harbor office.

Harbor office, quay side, open on weekdays.
